title: My First Week Without Snoozing
script: Narrator: [tired] My alarm used to ring at six, but I rarely stood up before half past six. I pressed the snooze button again and again.
Narrator: Those extra minutes did not make me feel rested. They made me rushed, and I often left home without breakfast.
Narrator: [determined] Last week, I tested a simple change. I put my phone on a shelf across the room before sleeping.
Narrator: When the alarm rang, I had to leave the bed to stop it. On the first morning, I nearly climbed back under the blanket.
Narrator: [tempted] Instead, I opened the curtains and drank the glass of water beside my desk. The light helped me wake up.
Narrator: I had prepared my clothes and bag the night before. Because of that, I did not need to make many decisions.
Narrator: [relieved] The second morning was still hard, but I had time to eat eggs and toast. I arrived at work ten minutes early.
Narrator: By Thursday, I noticed that my evenings also needed to change. Waking early is difficult when I watch videos until midnight.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I began charging my phone outside the bedroom at ten thirty. Then I read a few pages of a book and slept.
Narrator: On Friday morning, I woke a minute before the alarm. That felt surprising after years of fighting the snooze button.
Narrator: [surprised] One week does not mean the habit is permanent. I know there will be cold mornings when the bed feels especially comfortable.
Narrator: Still, I now understand that the solution is not stronger motivation at six o'clock. It is better preparation the night before.
Narrator: A distant phone, ready clothes, water, and an earlier bedtime make the morning choice easier.
Narrator: [calmly] My goal is not to become a perfect morning person. I simply want to begin the day without panic.

quiz.explanation: He repeatedly used the snooze button.

quiz.question: Where did he place his phone?
options: On a shelf across the room

quiz.explanation: Light and water helped him become alert.

quiz.question: What evening change did he make?
options: He charged the phone outside and slept earlier
quiz.explanation: He reduced late videos and moved the phone outside the room.

quiz.question: What is his real morning goal?
options: To become a famous morning person
quiz.explanation: He wants a calm start, not a perfect identity.

quiz.question: Why does the phone stay across the room?
options: He must stand to stop the alarm
quiz.explanation: Distance makes pressing snooze from bed impossible.

options: Delays the alarm for a short time
quiz.explanation: Repeated snoozing kept him in bed until he was rushed.

quiz.question: Which preparation reduced morning decisions?
options: Ready clothes and a packed bag
quiz.explanation: He had already chosen and packed important things.

quiz.question: Why did he change his evening videos?
options: Late watching made early waking harder
He wanted to read at work
quiz.explanation: An earlier bedtime supports the morning plan.

quiz.question: What does the narrator understand after one week?
options: One week makes a habit permanent
The night before shapes the morning
Breakfast is the only important change
quiz.explanation: Several evening choices make the early action easier.
